questions_and_answers.question_text: Which other word behaves the same way as -tian?
What form does the number 2 take when telling how many of something?
How do you say "one day" in Chinese?
What happens to the tone on yī before a High tone?
Write the Chinese for "She is staying two days."
Why is it liǎngtiān and not èrtiān?

answers.answer_text: Because when telling how many of something, the number 2 takes the form liǎng.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Which two words for time units are used without a counter?
Write the Chinese question meaning "How long is your wife staying?"
Compare the tone of yī in yìtiān and yìnián.

answers.answer_text: In both it is Falling — before the High tone of tiān and before the Rising tone of nián.

articles.text:
2. A: Nǐ tàitai zhù duō jiǔ?                How long is your wife staying?
   B: Tā zhù liǎngtiān.                     She is staying two days.

Note on No. 2

Liǎngtiān: -tian, "day," like -nián, "year," is used without a counter. When telling how many of something, the number 2 takes the form liǎng.* (See Unit 3, notes on Nos. 3-4.)

*"One day" is yìtiān. The tone on yī changes to Falling before a High tone.
